label: Peplink MAX BR2 Pro 5G router
description: Peplink MAX BR2 Pro (MAX-BR2-PRO-5GN-T-PRM) - ruggedised dual-5G SD-WAN router for vehicle and mobile deployments: 2x 2.5G Ethernet WAN (each convertible to LAN), 2x 5G modems with redundant SIM slots, 4x Gigabit Ethernet LAN, USB 3.0 WAN, simultaneous dual-band Wi-Fi 6 2x2 MU-MIMO as WAN and/or AP, a serial OOBM port, 802.3at PoE input, 10-30 V DC with ignition sensing, 12 W nominal and 30 W max, -40 to +65 C.
notes: The datasheet PDF enumerates the ports as text where the product page only draws them - 'WAN Interface: 2x 10/100/1000/2500M Ethernet' with '2x 5G Modems with Redundant SIM Slots' and '1x USB 3.0 Interface', 'LAN Interface: 4x 10/100/1000M Ethernet' - so the census is 2x 2.5G WAN + 4x 1G LAN + two 5G modems, plus a serial OOBM port named in the introduction ('The Gigabit routing speed and serial port for OOBM allow versatility'). **The WAN ports are faster than the LAN ports**, which is the unusual part: 2.5G on the WAN side against 1G on the LAN side, and footnote 1 adds 'The WAN port can act as a LAN port if needed' - recorded here rather than as five LAN ports. **PoE-in on one port only, flagged:** the datasheet says 'Power over Ethernet 802.3at' and footnote 5 says '802.3at PoE port provide a power supply of 25W', without naming the socket. It is declared on `wan1` and not on `wan2`, because two simultaneous feeds is something the footnote does not support; the whole point of the feature is 'one cable for both power and data' extending an SD-WAN link. **The 5G modems carry the datasheet's own theoretical maximum** ('5G: 4.1Gbps / 900Mbps') and are marked as such by the page itself ('Theoretical maximum data rates'), not presented as achievable throughput - the same 4.1G figure sits next to 'Router Throughput: 1 Gbps'. **Two radios, no rate:** 'Simultaneous Dual-Band (2.4GHz / 5GHz) Wi-Fi 6, 2X2 MU-MIMO' with Wi-Fi WAN and/or AP, so `wlan0` and `wlan1` are both radio interfaces with no `speed` - the datasheet never rates the radio. **Not modelled:** the USB 3.0 WAN port, because this catalogue has no USB interface type and inventing one for a single device would be worse than a note. Also absent by design: 'Redundant SIM slots' is a SIM switch inside each modem, not a second modem - the two `wwan` ports are the two actual modems.
